newsitem.title: USA: Inconsistencies in rape allegations by Army trainee.
newsitem.headline: Inconsistencies in rape allegations by Army trainee.

text.p: Several inconsistencies emerged in court on Tuesday between the oral testimony and the written statements of a woman Army trainee who said she was raped by her drill sergeant at Aberdeen Proving Ground.

The defence attorney for Staff Sgt. Delmar Simpson, who was charged by the Army with 19 counts of rape and 39 other offences including indecent exposure, battery and maltreatment involving 13 women, closely questioned the woman about the inconsistencies during court-martial proceedings.
Capt. Edward Brady asked the woman, whose name has not been published, why her testimony in open court on Monday differed from her written statement.
The woman said that an investigator typed her statement, sometimes interpreting what she was saying.
"The words that he typed weren't slang words. They were more direct words," she said.
Then Brady read from her statement: "'Yes, he penetrated my vagina with his penis.' You never said that did you?" She answered, "no."
On Monday she had testified that Simpson had "made me sleep with him."

Brady then asked if it surprised her "if some of the agents tell the truth and others don't." "No," she said. "It wouldn't surprise me what anything or anybody says or does anymore. He (Simpson) was supposed to be my leader. I was supposed to trust him."

Simpson's defence attorneys said earlier that prosecutors and investigators had heaped charges on Simpson. The defence unsuccessfully argued that the case be dismissed because the Army's public handling of the sex scandal tainted its ability to hold a fair trial.

The alleged rape victim testified on Monday that Simpson called her to his office, presumably for violating a bedtime curfew, pushed her down onto a couch, pulled her shorts down, put his hands over her mouth and raped her.

Two more women testified that Simpson made advances and asked for sex when they were alone with him in his office. One woman said she found herself backed up against the corner trying to avoid his kiss.
"I was kind of nervous with the way the situation was heading," the second woman said.
She said Simpson asked to have oral sex with her. She said she replied that she was here to finish her training and "not to have sex with my drill sergeant."
The next day she said, "he actually said he was going to leave me alone."

Another woman, now a specialist who joined the Army at age 26, said Simpson would not take no for an answer. The woman, said she was having a hard enough time dealing with basic training in the first two weeks at Aberdeen when Simpson started making his advances.
"I explained to him (that) like a boss in the civilian world, I would do nothing with him. It just knocked me off my feet. I wasn't expecting it because I didn't think of him in that way."

She said she joined a softball team "even though I couldn't play that well, to keep away from Simpson." But during a dinner, she found herself next to Simpson who whispered that he wanted to have oral sex with her. She went to the bathroom to try to compose herself.
When asked what she thought of Simpson, she said, "I couldn't stand him."
